presentation.selected_title: Local Coding Agents: Estimate Time per Turn, Not Just Tokens/s
presentation.title_rationale: The reader's problem is a local coding agent that times out mid-task while chat answers feel fast, so the title frontloads the product ('Local Coding Agents') and names the supported benefit: estimate time per turn instead of trusting one tokens-per-second figure. 'Estimate' is what the article actually delivers - an equation, a worked example on upstream benchmark rows and a harness - and the 'Not Just Tokens/s' contrast is the article's own thesis, not an exaggerated fix. At 62 characters it drops the previous 107-character version, which buried the unit behind a clause about what a tokens/second figure buys you.
presentation.visual_purpose: A three-step conceptual checklist of the phases that make up one agent turn: prompt prefill, then output decoding, then client-side tool overhead. It exists so a reader sees the additive structure before estimating a multi-turn run. Scope: it is a label-only diagram of the terms in the article's turn equation and prints no numbers, shares or timings, so it cannot be read as a measurement or as a hardware comparison.
